results.title: Performant local mixture-of-experts CPU inference with GPU acceleration in llama.cpp
results.content:
So you want to try one of those fancy huge mixture-of-experts (MoE) models locally? Well, whether you've got a gaming PC or a large multi-GPU workstation, we've got you covered. As long as you've downloaded enough RAM beforehand.

## Anatomy of a MoE Model

MoE models are described in terms of their total parameters and active parameters - i.e. DeepSeek V3 671B A37B has 671B total parameters, but we are using only 37B parameters at a time during each forward pass through the model. [...] In their current form (i.e. DeepSeek V3, GLM 4.X, Kimi K2, Qwen 3 MoE), they contain several major components (for the sake of simplicity):

The first three are "always active" in the sense that these model parameters are being used in every forward pass through the model. The last component, the routed experts, take up the vast majority of the model's total size, but we only activate a fraction of these parameters during each forward pass.

## Optimizing CPU offloading in llama.cpp [...] Or use the built in function:

`--n-cpu-moe 31`

Note: `--n-cpu-moe` starts counting layers starting from the highest numbered layers. This can lead to a slightly discrepancy in how many layers are offloaded because models that have Dense FFN layers typically have them at the start of the model (i.e. the first 3 layers of DeepSeek V3).

`--n-cpu-moe`

If you have multiple GPUs, you can specify layers to assign to each device:

`-ot "blk\.([0-9])\.=CUDA0,blk\.(1[0-9])\.=CUDA1,exps=CPU"`

results.title: Feature Request: MoE only load activated expert(s) to GPU while rest non-used experts are not loaded (to CPU/GPU) for DeekSeek-R1 Inference on consumer GPU · Issue #11532 · ggml-org/llama.cpp · GitHub
results.content:
Running DeekSeep-R1 or V3 inference needs 8xH100 80GB due to huge memory footprint, and it's very challenging to do R1 or V3 inference on single consumer GPU RAM (e.g. 24GB 4090) + limited CPU memory (say 32GB) with 685B MoE params even with low-bit quantization. [...] I'm wondering if similar features is available or WIP inside llama.cpp or any other popular inference frameworks ?

Really appreciate your help!

### Motivation

This will help llama.cpp users to run DeepSeek-R1, the best reasoning LLM by far, which has 685B MoE param but only 37B activated param, on consumer GPU device (4090 24GB) plus consumer CPU (i7/i9 32GB mem), with low-bit quantization, with an acceptable inference speed.

### Possible Implementation

No response

## Metadata [...] DeepSeek-R1 MoE has 61 layers, current llama implementation will load n-gpu-layers of MoE to GPU memory (say 7 layers on 24GB 4090) while remaining layers of weights all on CPU memory, but when CPU only has limited memory (say 32GB), there will be huge swapping and make the inference speed extremely slow. but if we only load the "activated" expert (37B), it can fit into single 24GB 4090, also no need to do expensive swapping for unused expert on CPU memory/disk, i expect the 685B DeepSeek-R1

results.title: Local DeepSeek-R1 671B on $800 configurations
results.content: The MoE (Mixture of Experts) architecture’s tens of billions of active parameters make it feasible to further enhance performance by adding tens (<50) of gigabytes of high-speed memory (VRAM) and corresponding compute power (via GPU or AMX). This is exactly the architecture used in ktransformers. There are many GPU options that can support this setup — we’ll be conducting experiments and sharing our analysis soon. Stay tuned! [...] No matter how competitors attack DeepSeek, the V3 and R1 models are fully open-source LLMs with capabilities rivaling various commercial models. You can inspect every line of its code, run it on a completely offline machine, and fine-tune any “bias” in its output that you find unsatisfactory — making it far more controllable and secure than models like ChatGPT, Gemini, or Claude. Moreover, its advanced MoE architecture frees inference from the need for data center-level computing power.
